newsitem.title: CANADA: Ethyl says Canada mum on possible MMT lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Ethyl says Canada mum on possible MMT lawsuit.

text.p: Ethyl Corp, which has threatened the Canadian government with a US$200 million lawsuit over a proposed ban of the gasoline additive MMT, on Thursday said Ottawa has not responded to its call for a discussion.

"Exactly one month has elapsed since Ethyl Corp filed a notice of intent to submit a NAFTA claim ... and there has been no attempt on part of the government to open discussions," Ethyl said in a press release.

A month ago, Richmond, Va.-based Ethyl said it would sue the Canadian government under the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) in a bid to stop the bill which aims to ban the import and interprovincial trade of MMT.
MMT, methylcyclopentadienyl manganese tricarbonyl, is a fuel octane enhancer. It has been used as a replacement for lead in gasoline in Canada since 1977.

Ethyl's filing of notice of intent started a 90-day consultation process between the company and the government, but Canadian Environment Minister Sergio Marchi has said he saw little point in meeting Ethyl again.
Ethyl's Canadian subsidiary, Ethyl Canada is the sole importer and manufacturer of MMT in the country.
The bill is awaiting a final hearing and vote in Canada's House of Commons.

The use of MMT in the United States has been permitted since late 1995 after a U.S. Court of Appeals overruled Environmental Protection Agency objections to the additive. --Malina Poshtova Zang, Reuters Ottawa Bureau (613) 235-6745
